newsitem.title: TURKEY: New tax seen reducing demand for Turkish fx bonds.
newsitem.headline: New tax seen reducing demand for Turkish fx bonds.

text.p: A newly imposed 10 percent witholding tax on interest income from government securities is expected to reduce demand for the Turkish Treasury's current hard currency bond issue, bankers said.

"The witholding tax will lower the return on these bonds. The Treasury's call for bids also came at short notice. There was not enough time to fully inform foreign investors," said a private bank treasury official.

The Treasury asked banks late on Thursday for bids by Friday's close for its new offer of dollar and mark bonds having three-year maturity and interest payments every six months. It is the second such issue since September.
The interest rates will be London Interbank Offered Rate plus 2.6 points on the dollar-denominated bonds and Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate plus two points on the mark bonds.
The government imposed the 10 percent witholding tax on interest earnings from t-bills and bonds to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1.
"The currency bonds may be of interest for state and big private banks, but for small banks, it is difficult to take such a position for such a long time," said a senior banker.
The minimun amount of participation will be $10 million or 15 million marks.
The Treasury sold $1.12 billion of similar bonds on September 25, the first issue of such papers planned as part of the Islamist-led government's first revenue raising package revealed on July 31.
